docs.title: Job Application Assistant
docs.text: A sophisticated multi-agent job application automation system built on Google's Agent Development Kit (ADK). This system automates the complete job application workflow: scraping jobs from multiple sites, creating Google Drive folders with resumes, generating tailored cover letters, and submitting applications.

docs.title: 🏗️ System Architecture
docs.text: User Input → Orchestrator Agent → Specialized Sub-Agents → Database & Google Drive

docs.title: Agent Hierarchy
docs.text:
orchestrator_agent (LlmAgent)
├── job_scraper_agent (scrapes from 5+ sites)
├── resource_manager_agent (creates folders, copies resumes)
│   └── batch_resource_manager (handles bulk folder operations)
├── content_generator_agent (analyzes fit, writes cover letters)
│   └── batch_content_generator (handles >25 jobs with rate limiting)
├── database_agent (database operations)
├── application_submitter_agent (automated submissions)
│   └── batch_submitter (sequential job applications)
└── email_assistant_agent (email classification)

docs.title: 🔑 Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-Site Job Scraping: LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, Google Jobs
  • Smart Deduplication: Prevents duplicate applications across sites
  • Chrome Extension: Manual job saving from any website with one-click integration
  • Google Drive Integration: Automated folder creation and document management
  • AI Content Generation: Personalized cover letters using Gemini models And Resumes
  • Browser Automation: Headless job application submission with CAPTCHA solving
  • Email Classification: Process job-related emails automatically
  • Batch Processing: Handle large volumes with rate limiting

docs.title: Application Submitter Agent
docs.text: The Application Submitter Agent is responsible for automatically submitting job applications on LinkedIn and Google Jobs using Browser Use automation. It processes jobs marked as "Ready To Apply" in the database using a subprocess-based approach that ensures complete Chrome isolation between jobs to prevent 429 rate limiting errors.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Orchestrator Agent
    └── Batch Submitter Agent (orchestration layer)
            ├── linkedin_submitter.py (subprocess execution)
            │       ├── Chrome Process Management (fresh instance per job)
            │       ├── Browser Use CDP Connection
            │       ├── Controller Actions (file uploads, Gmail verification)
            │       └── Database Updates
            └── google_submitter.py (subprocess execution)
                    ├── Chrome Process Management (fresh instance per job)
                    ├── Browser Use CDP Connection
                    ├── Controller Actions (file uploads, navigation)
                    └── Database Updates

docs.title: Key Change: Subprocess Isolation
docs.text: Each job runs in a completely separate Python process, ensuring: - Chrome fully terminates between jobs (prevents context pollution) - Fresh browser state for each application (avoids 429 errors) - Exact replication of test script behavior - Clean memory and connection state

docs.title: Subprocess Execution Model
docs.text:
batch_submitter.py → subprocess.run() → linkedin_submitter.py <job_id>
                                    └──→ google_submitter.py <job_id>

docs.title: 1. Batch Processing
docs.text:
• Batch Submitter fetches jobs with "Ready To Apply" status
  • Routes jobs to appropriate submitter based on submitter_tool field
  • Processes one job at a time with 30-second cooldowns
  • Each job runs in isolated subprocess

docs.title: 2. Subprocess Execution
docs.text:
# Run appropriate submitter based on job source
if job['submitter_tool'] == 'linkedin_submitter':
    subprocess.run([python_path, "linkedin_submitter.py", str(job_id)])
elif job['submitter_tool'] == 'google_submitter':
    subprocess.run([python_path, "google_submitter.py", str(job_id)])

docs.title: 3. Chrome Lifecycle (Per Job)
docs.text:
1. Start fresh Chrome instance with Browser Use profile
  2. Connect via CDP on port 9222
  3. Execute job submission
  4. Terminate Chrome completely (pkill)
  5. Exit subprocess cleanly

docs.title: LinkedIn Submitter:
docs.text:
• Downloads resume/cover letter from Google Drive
  • Connects to Chrome via CDP
  • Navigates to LinkedIn job URL
  • Handles multi-step Easy Apply process
  • Uploads documents and fills forms
  • Submits application

docs.title: Google Jobs Submitter:
docs.text:
• Downloads resume/cover letter from Google Drive
  • Connects to Chrome via CDP
  • Navigates to Google Jobs URL
  • Extracts and follows Apply button to company site
  • Handles various application portals (Greenhouse, Lever, etc.)
  • Uploads documents and fills forms
  • Submits application

docs.title: 5. Controller Actions
docs.text: Shared browser actions (in browser_actions/shared_browser_actions.py): - Resume/cover letter content extraction (PDF support) - File uploads to application forms - Gmail verification code/URL retrieval - Database status updates - Personal information provision - Apply button detection and clicking - Navigation to application URLs - CAPTCHA handling with 2captcha integration

docs.title: 6. Status Updates
docs.text: Ready To Apply → Application in Progress → Applied/Error/Not a Fit

docs.title: Batch Submitter (batch_submitter.py)
docs.text:
• ADK BaseAgent that orchestrates job processing
  • Runs each job as isolated subprocess
  • 30-second cooldowns between jobs
  • Handles subprocess communication via JSON
  • Tracks success/failure statistics

docs.title: LinkedIn Submitter (tools/linkedin_submitter.py)
docs.text: Standalone script that: 1. Takes job ID as command line argument 2. Fetches job data from database 3. Downloads resume/cover letter from Google Drive 4. Starts Chrome with Browser Use profile 5. Connects via CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) 6. Runs Browser Use agent for LinkedIn Easy Apply 7. Terminates Chrome completely 8. Returns JSON result via stdout

docs.title: Google Submitter (tools/google_submitter.py)
docs.text: Standalone script that: 1. Takes job ID as command line argument 2. Fetches job data from database 3. Downloads resume/cover letter from Google Drive 4. Starts Chrome with Browser Use profile 5. Connects via CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) 6. Runs Browser Use agent for external application sites 7. Terminates Chrome completely 8. Returns JSON result via stdout

docs.title: 🚨 Important Notes
docs.text:
1. Browser Use Profile: Uses ~/.config/browseruse/profiles/default-google-chrome (NOT personal Chrome profile)
  2. Chrome Termination: Each job terminates Chrome completely to prevent 429 errors
  3. Subprocess Isolation: Each job runs in separate Python process for clean state
  4. Real-time Logs: Subprocess output streams to console while also saving to log files
  5. CDP Connection: Connects to existing Chrome instance instead of Browser Use spawning it
  6. No Process Management in ADK: Chrome lifecycle handled by subprocess exit, not ADK
  7. Shared Browser Actions: Both submitters use consolidated actions from browser_actions/shared_browser_actions.py
  8. Platform Support: Supports jobs from LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, and Google Jobs

docs.title: Content Generator Agent
docs.text: The Content Generator Agent is responsible for analyzing job fit and generating tailored cover letters for qualified positions. It processes jobs that have been prepared by the Resource Manager (with folders and resumes already in place) and determines which jobs David should apply to based on his experience and the job requirements.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The Content Generator has two modes of operation:

1. Regular Mode (≤25 jobs):
   Orchestrator → Content Generator Agent → Direct Processing

2. Batch Mode (>25 jobs):
   Orchestrator → Batch Content Generator → Content Worker (per batch)
                     ├── Batch 1 (25 jobs) → 60s cooldown
                     ├── Batch 2 (25 jobs) → 60s cooldown
                     └── Batch N (remaining jobs)

docs.title: 📁 Directory Structure
docs.text:
content_generator_agent/
├── __init__.py               # Exports content_generator_agent
├── agent.py                  # Regular agent for ≤25 jobs
├── batch_content_generator.py # Custom BaseAgent for >25 jobs
├── prompt.py                 # All prompts (regular and batch)
├── readme.md                 # This file
└── tests/
    ├── conftest.py           # Pytest fixtures (real components)
    ├── test_content_generator.py       # Tests for regular agent
    ├── test_batch_content_generator.py # Tests for batch agent
    └── run_tests.py          # Test runner

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Jobs must be in "Pending Review" status
  • Each job must have:
  • drive_folder_id (created by Resource Manager)
  • resume_link (copied by Resource Manager)
  • role_type (engineer or product)

docs.title: Processing Steps
docs.text:
1. Retrieve Jobs 

    get_jobs_ready_for_content() → Returns jobs with folders & resumes

  2. For Each Job:

  3. Get full job details including role_type
  4. Select appropriate resume (engineer vs product)
  5. Analyze job fit based on David's experience
  6. If qualified: Generate cover letter

  7. If not qualified: Reject with specific reason

  8. Document Creation (if qualified)

  9. Generate personalized cover letter content
  10. Create Google Doc in existing folder
  11. Convert to PDF

  12. Update database with document links

  13. Status Updates 

    Pending Review → Ready To Apply (qualified)
Pending Review → Not a Fit (rejected)

docs.title: Auto-Accept Roles
docs.text:

  • Product Management: Technical Product Manager, AI Product Manager
  • Senior Engineering: Senior Python Developer, Tech Lead

  • Fintech: Any finance/trading technology roles

docs.title: Auto-Reject Criteria
docs.text:
• Non-US locations
  • Non-English job descriptions
  • Requires 20+ years experience
  • Completely different fields (doctor, lawyer)
  • Entry-level only positions
  • Pure ML Engineer roles (PyTorch/TensorFlow from scratch)

docs.title: Remote Work Policy
docs.text:
Accept as remote-friendly: - Remote-first, Fully remote, 100% remote - Hybrid, Distributed team - Occasional offsites are OK

Reject only if: - On-site only - In-office required daily/weekly - Specific city with no remote option

docs.title: Database Agent
docs.text: The Database Agent serves as the single source of truth for all job tracking data and the primary interface between the orchestrator and the SQLite database. It handles all database operations and provides structured responses to orchestrator queries.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Orchestrator → Database Agent → SQLite Database (linkedin_jobs.db)
                    ↓
            Other agents receive 
            database state info

The Database Agent follows a strict pattern where: - Only it can directly interact with the database - Other agents request data through the orchestrator - All database operations are atomic and validated

├── readme.md       # This file

Common queries:

-- Find stuck jobs

AND updated_at < datetime('now', '-1 hour');

-- Check for duplicates

FROM jobs GROUP BY company_name, job_title

docs.title: 🚨 Important Notes
docs.text:

  2. Status Validation: Invalid status transitions are rejected
  3. Atomic Operations: All updates are transactional
  4. No Direct Access: Other agents must go through orchestrator
  5. Data Integrity: Foreign keys and constraints are enforced

docs.title: Email Assistant Agent
docs.text: The Email Assistant Agent is an intelligent email classification system that monitors your Gmail inbox for job application-related emails. It automatically categorizes, labels, and tracks correspondence in the database, turning your chaotic inbox into an organized job search command center.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Orchestrator Agent
    └── Email Assistant Agent
            ├── Gmail API Integration
            ├── LLM-Based Classification Engine
            ├── Label Management System
            └── Database Correspondence Tracking

docs.title: Key Innovation: Intelligent Classification
docs.text:
• Uses LLM understanding, not keyword matching
  • Analyzes full email context (sender, subject, body)
  • Makes nuanced decisions about edge cases
  • Learns from email patterns and formats

docs.title: 📁 Directory Structure
docs.text:
email_assistant_agent/
├── __init__.py
├── agent.py                   # LLM agent with classification logic
├── prompt.py                  # Intelligent classification instructions
├── scripts/                   # Utility scripts
│   └── export_emails_for_review.py  # Export emails for analysis
└── tests/                     # Test suite
    ├── conftest.py
    ├── test_email_classification.py
    └── run_email_agent.py

docs.title: Classification Pipeline
docs.text: Inbox → Fetch Unprocessed → LLM Analysis → Apply Label → Archive → Update Database

docs.title: 1. Email Discovery
docs.text:
• Searches for emails without job-related labels
  • Query: is:inbox -label:applied-jobs -label:further-action -label:rejects -label:job-advertisements
  • Processes up to 50 emails per run (configurable)

docs.title: 2. Intelligent Classification
docs.text: The LLM analyzes each email to determine: - Context: Who sent it? What company? What's the purpose? - Intent: Is action required? Is this a rejection? A confirmation? - Category: Which label best fits this email?

docs.title: 📬 applied-jobs
docs.text:
• Application confirmations
  • "Thank you for applying" messages
  • Submission receipts
  • Verification codes sent during application

docs.title: 🎯 further-action
docs.text:
• Interview invitations
  • Assessment requests
  • Recruiter questions requiring response
  • Document requests
  • Scheduling links

docs.title: ❌ rejects
docs.text:
• Explicit rejection notifications
  • "Position filled" messages
  • "Not moving forward" decisions
  • "Pursuing other candidates" emails

docs.title: 📢 job-advertisements
docs.text:
• Job alerts and recommendations
  • New opportunity notifications
  • Job board newsletters
  • "You might be interested in" emails

docs.title: 📥 Inbox (No Label)
docs.text:
• Emails that don't fit any category
  • Personal emails
  • Non-job-related content

docs.title: 4. Database Integration
docs.text: For rejects and further-action emails: - Extracts company name intelligently - Matches to existing job records - Updates correspondence history - Tracks all communication threads

docs.title: 5. Results Summary
docs.text: Provides detailed statistics: - Total emails processed - Breakdown by category - Sample emails from each category - Any processing errors

docs.title: LLM Agent (agent.py)
docs.text:
• Uses Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash model
  • Processes emails individually for accuracy
  • Makes intelligent classification decisions
  • Tracks statistics in memory

docs.title: Classification Prompt (prompt.py)
docs.text: Guides the LLM through: 1. Reading full email context 2. Understanding sender intent 3. Determining appropriate category 4. Extracting company/job information 5. Generating classification summary

docs.title: Gmail Integration
docs.text:
• OAuth2 authentication
  • Batch operations for efficiency
  • Label creation and management
  • Email archiving (removes from inbox)

docs.title: Database Functions
docs.text:
• find_and_update_job_correspondence() - Links emails to job records
  • Smart matching by company name
  • Handles ambiguous matches gracefully
  • Maintains correspondence history

docs.title: Smart Context Analysis
docs.text: The agent understands: - Sender patterns: no-reply@greenhouse.io → likely job-related - Subject analysis: "Update on your application" → needs classification - Body content: Looks for intent, not just keywords - Email structure: Automated vs personal communication

docs.title: Edge Case Handling
docs.text:
• Ambiguous rejections: "We'll keep your resume on file"
  • Delayed responses: "We're still reviewing applications"
  • Multi-purpose emails: Rejection + job recommendations
  • False positives: "Thank you" in rejection emails

docs.title: Job Scraper Agent
docs.text: The Job Scraper Agent is responsible for finding and importing job opportunities from multiple job sites including LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter, and Google Jobs. It uses a combination of JobSpy integration and professional APIs to gather job listings while avoiding duplicates.

docs.title: 🏗️ Architecture Overview
docs.text:
Orchestrator → Job Scraper Agent → Independent Scrapers
                                        ├── LinkedIn (JobSpy)
                                        ├── Indeed (JobSpy/Apify)
                                        ├── Glassdoor (JobSpy)
                                        ├── ZipRecruiter (JobSpy)
                                        └── Google Jobs (SerpAPI)
                                              ↓
                                        Database (via callbacks)

docs.title: 📁 Directory Structure
docs.text:
job_scraper_agent/
├── __init__.py              # Exports job_scraper_agent
├── agent.py                 # Main LlmAgent definition
├── prompt.py                # Agent instructions
├── independent_scrapers.py  # Core scraping logic
├── site_agents/            # Per-site agent configurations (unused)
├── tools/                  # Professional API integrations
│   ├── apify_indeed_scraper.py      # Apify for Indeed
│   ├── serpapi_google_jobs_scraper.py # SerpAPI for Google
│   └── serpapi_usage_tracker.py      # API usage monitoring
└── tests/                  # Pytest tests with real data
    ├── test_independent_scrapers.py
    ├── test_jobspy_integration.py
    └── ... (various integration tests)

docs.title: 1. Duplicate Prevention
docs.text: get_applied_urls_by_role_type() → Returns URLs already applied to

docs.title: 2. Site Selection
docs.text: Agent supports single-site or multi-site scraping: - Single: source="linkedin" - Multi: source="all" → LinkedIn + Indeed + Glassdoor

docs.title: 3. Scraping Process
docs.text: For each site: 1. Get site-specific scraper function 2. Execute with parameters (query, location, max_jobs) 3. Filter duplicates against applied URLs 4. Store new jobs in database with "Pending Review" status

docs.title: 4. Error Handling
docs.text:
• Continues on site failures
  • Reports per-site results
  • Aggregates total jobs found

docs.title: Resource Manager Agent
docs.text: This module handles the creation of Google Drive folders and copying of role-specific resumes for job applications.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Resource Manager is responsible for: - Creating company-specific folders in Google Drive - Copying the appropriate resume (engineer vs product) based on job role - Converting documents to PDF format - Updating the database with folder and document links

docs.title: 1. Regular Resource Manager (agent.py)
docs.text:
• Use case: Processing ≤50 jobs
  • Agent type: LlmAgent
  • Processes: Jobs one at a time with natural conversation flow
  • Status flow: Jobs remain in "Pending Review" after processing

docs.title: 2. Batch Resource Manager (batch_resource_manager.py)
docs.text:
• Use case: Processing >50 jobs
  • Agent type: BaseAgent with internal LlmAgent worker
  • Batch size: 50 jobs per batch
  • Rate limiting: 60-second cooldown between batches
  • Error handling: Extended 90-second cooldown on Google Drive API rate limits

docs.title: 3. Junior Resource Manager (agent.py)
docs.text:
• Use case: Simplified version optimized for Gemini 2.0
  • Features: Also handles cleanup of rejected job folders

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
The orchestrator automatically selects the appropriate resource manager:

User: "resource"
→ Orchestrator calls get_jobs_needing_resources()
→ If ≤50 jobs: Uses resource_manager_agent
→ If >50 jobs: Uses batch_resource_manager

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Job Detection: Find jobs with status "Pending Review" that lack resume links
  2. Folder Creation: Create a Google Drive folder named "{Company} - {Job Title}"
  3. Resume Selection: Determine role type (engineer/product) and get appropriate resume
  4. Document Copying: Copy resume to company folder with applicant name
  5. PDF Conversion: Convert Google Docs to PDF format
  6. Database Update: Save folder ID, resume links, and PDF links

docs.title: Smart Batch Processing
docs.text:
• Processes large job queues without hitting API rate limits
  • Automatic retry with extended cooldowns on rate limit errors
  • Progress tracking and reporting between batches

docs.title: Role-Based Resume Selection
docs.text:
• Automatically detects job role type from job title
  • Selects appropriate resume folder based on role
  • Falls back to engineer resume as default

docs.title: State Management
docs.text:
• Uses ADK memory functions (memorize/recall_all) for session state
  • Shares state between orchestrator and sub-agents
  • Batch context passed via session state

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
1. Memory Functions: Never wrap memorize or recall_all in FunctionTool (causes ADK errors)
  2. Status Updates: Jobs stay in "Pending Review" after resource processing
  3. Content Generator Dependency: Content generator expects jobs to have resume links before processing
  4. Rate Limits: Google Drive API has quotas - batch processor handles this automatically

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Missing resume folders: Falls back to engineer resume
  • API rate limits: Automatic cooldown and retry
  • Failed folder creation: Job remains unprocessed for next batch
  • Database errors: Transaction rollback to maintain consistency

docs.title: database.py
docs.text:
Central database operations module handling all SQLite interactions.

Key Functions: - Job Management - add_job() - Add new scraped job - update_job_status() - Update job status in pipeline - get_job_details() - Get complete job information - get_jobs_by_status() - Retrieve jobs by status

  • Application Tracking
  • reserve_job_for_application() - Atomic job reservation
  • update_job_status_applied() - Mark job as applied
  • release_job_reservation() - Release failed reservation

  • get_applied_urls_by_role_type() - Duplicate prevention

  • Resource Management

  • get_jobs_needing_resources() - Jobs without folders/resumes
  • update_job_folder_id() - Store Google Drive folder ID

  • get_job_folder_id() - Quick folder lookup

  • Content Generation

  • get_jobs_ready_for_content() - Jobs with resources ready
  • reject_job_with_reason() - Mark job as not qualified
  • get_jobs_by_content_level() - Filter by content needs

Database Schema: 

CREATE TABLE jobs (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    company_name TEXT NOT NULL,
    job_title TEXT NOT NULL,
    job_url TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
    job_description TEXT,
    application_status TEXT DEFAULT 
    role_type TEXT, 
    drive_folder_id TEXT,
    resume_link TEXT,
    cover_letter_link TEXT,
    applied_date TEXT,
    rejection_reason TEXT,
    -- timestamps and metadata
)

docs.title: memory.py
docs.text:
ADK callback system for state management between agents.

Key Callbacks: - populate_job_scraper_state() - Setup scraping parameters - scraping_results_callback() - Process scraping results - populate_resource_manager_state() - Setup resource creation - populate_content_generator_state() - Setup content generation - memorize() / recall_all() - State persistence

State Flow Example: 

# Orchestrator sets:
session.state['job_title'] = 'Python Developer'
session.state['content_level'] = 'cover_letter_only'

# Sub-agents access via callbacks:
def populate_job_scraper_state(ctx):
    job_title = ctx.session.state.get('job_title')
    # Use for scraping...

docs.text:
